import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures associated with A109909

$a(n)$ = number of primes of the form $k(n-k)-1$.

*References:*
- [A109909](https://oeis.org/A109909)
-/

namespace OeisA109909

/--
$a(n)$ is the number of primes of the form $k(n-k)-1$.
This counts the number of distinct prime values in the set $\{k(n-k)-1 | 1 \le k < n\}$.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.Ico 1 n).image (fun k => k * (n - k) - 1)
  |>.filter Nat.Prime
  |>.card

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 2 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 2 := by decide

/--
Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for $n > 3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : ∀ n > 3, a n > 0 := by
  sorry

end OeisA109909

reformulations.difference: OEIS gives the expression k*(n-k)-1 without explicit bounds on k. Lean counts its distinct prime values over natural k with 1 ≤ k < n, using natural-number subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 0, an integer representation of a positive prime forces k*(n-k) > 0, hence 0 < k < n. On this interval, k ≤ n and k*(n-k) ≥ 1, so both natural-number subtractions agree with integer subtraction. Finset.image removes duplicate representations rather than counting them twice. In the scratch file, proved the exact equality between a n and the cardinality of {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ ∃ k : ℤ, (p : ℤ) = k*((n : ℤ)-k)-1}. Also proved that the full interval and 1 ≤ k ≤ n/2 have identical images.

review.notes: Checked all seven declarations: a, a_1–a_5, and conjecture. Lean evaluation matches all 93 published sequence terms; the five test statements and the additional boundary case a 0 = 0 were checked. Sorry-free scratch proofs establish the counting equivalence and positivity iff a prime value exists. The source explicitly states “Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for n > 3,” exactly matching conjecture. Both accessible OEIS entries still call it a conjecture and report verification up to 10^9. ResearchGate blocked the linked 2024 Niu–Zhang preprint, so its full text could not be independently checked for further status information. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the reviewed file was not modified.
